modules.name: Regulated-Industry Mode
modules.purpose: Apply a five-part compliance bundle as one setting, and enforce each constituent uniformly across the Hub.

modules.name: Standard Report Data Sets (5)
modules.purpose: Own and compute the five date- and scope-filterable data sets the platform reports against.

modules.name: Parts Registry
modules.purpose: Hold the tenant's part master data so work instructions can reference parts and genealogy can record what was consumed.

modules.name: Charter and Position
modules.purpose: Establish and enforce the Studio's authority boundary: enable, configure, compose; never define

modules.name: Agent Configuration
modules.purpose: Supply each standard agent with the operating parameters it requires, carried inside authored Workflow content

modules.name: Workflow Library and Tenant Workspace
modules.purpose: Hold, classify, filter, and expose the tenant's complete Workflow inventory with authoring status, version, and linkage

modules.name: Workflow Builder
modules.purpose: Set Workflow-level settings and defaults, and assemble the screen sequence and branch targets that are simultaneously the worker's path and the sequence-detection reference

modules.name: Screen Authoring and the Nine Configuration Sections
modules.purpose: Configure every screen the worker meets, supplying each agent capability with the information it requires

modules.name: Shared Instruction Blocks
modules.purpose: Author instruction context once at Workflow level and apply it to any number of screens within that Workflow

modules.name: Content Libraries
modules.purpose: Hold the tenant's reusable containment checklists, approved coaching assets, and escalation routing templates, referenced by pointer from screens

modules.name: Training Library
modules.purpose: Author, version, and publish long-form instructional content delivered online-only and excluded from the offline work package

modules.name: Work-Instruction Difficulty Levels
modules.purpose: Provide three reviewed renderings of the same instruction content so each worker reads at the depth that suits them, without any variation in what the platform enforces

modules.name: Parts-Registry Authoring Seam
modules.purpose: Let an author reference a part that does not yet exist without leaving the authoring context or stalling on master data

modules.name: Approval Workflow
modules.purpose: Enforce three-stage human sign-off with separation of duties on every piece of content that reaches the frontline

modules.name: Versioning and Publication
modules.purpose: Mint, classify, describe, distribute, compare, archive, and export Workflow versions, and make the version number the audit receipt for which limits were in force

modules.name: Qualification Requirements
modules.purpose: State authoritatively which certifications a Workflow and its individual screens require, at two levels, validated at three points

modules.name: The Offline Package
modules.purpose: Define, build, deliver, and pin the complete self-sufficient bundle a device needs to render, evaluate, and enforce a Run alone

modules.name: The Agent Builder
modules.purpose: Enable atomic capabilities within entitlement and compose, evaluate, approve, deploy, and map tenant reasoning agents

modules.name: Memory and the Two-Lane Learning Loop
modules.purpose: Write the Studio's authored content into memory, refine selection automatically inside authored boundaries, and route any proposed change to a configured value through a single human decision

modules.name: Localisation
modules.purpose: Hold per-locale authored variants inside one Workflow and block publication in any locale whose worker-facing content is incomplete

modules.name: Permissions and Roles in the Studio
modules.purpose: Gate every Studio capability by role and grant, and enforce a separation-of-duties floor that no tenant can widen

business_rules.statement: Regulated-Industry mode is a single per-tenant toggle, set from the Super Admin platform console, bundling five constituents — each also independently settable.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Super Admin platform console; Delivery Operations Hub enforcement

business_rules.statement: Switching a tenant into Regulated-Industry mode later does not, and cannot, restore already-anonymised identities. Anonymisation is the platform's one irreversible act.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Lifecycle service; mode-status view; platform console change point

business_rules.statement: An unreadable mode flag is treated as on, and the tenant is told the posture is precautionary. Stricter interpretation applies because treating a regulated tenant as unregulated is the more dangerous error.

The Delivery Operations Hub owns the data behind the five standard report data sets; rendering, layout, saved formats and scheduled delivery are Client Command Center capabilities through the Custom Report Builder.
business_rules.enforcement_point: MOD-DOH-18 / Client Command Center Custom Report Builder

business_rules.statement: Reports are never presented as real-time; each carries its data-as-of timestamp. Late-arriving data that materially changes delivered figures is corrected in the next scheduled delivery, flagged as corrections.
No sixth data set, no new data domain and no outbound delivery into tenant systems is possible at V1.

Manufacturing-execution-domain constructs — bill of materials, recipe, stock-keeping unit, routing — are deliberately not first-class platform entities; they are captured as Data Capture entries inside workflow steps.

No part number is ever typed on the floor. Consumption is referenced through the work-instruction step. Identification is entirely optional per client and per part: track as much as possible, force nothing.
A bulk upload is all-or-nothing per file and produces a per-row error report on rejection.
During a connectivity loss, mobile devices continue offline and sync on recovery — the operational edge protocol is about visibility, not stopping the floor.
A device timestamp outside the tenant's clock-skew threshold is not trusted to order writes and always routes to human resolution in the Client Command Center conflict-review panel.
A worker logging in on an unexpected device is allowed at V1 and flagged in the audit trail; there is no hard block. Attribution follows the login, never the device.
A worker correction after submission is an append-only correction record: the original is immutable, with full who, when and what-changed. On a finished run, the audited-recompute rule applies.
Archival is manual only at V1; auto-archival of stale entities is deferred beyond V1. No entity is auto-archived at V1.
No conflict is ever resolved by discarding a version silently.
Every value is validated against the Super Admin tenant-configuration registry: the platform rejects, rather than logs, any value looser than the platform floor. Tenants tighten; they never loosen.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Tenant administration area write path; FB-DOH-WRITE-002

business_rules.statement: Tenant Administration is not a sixth surface. It is the Tenant Admin's screen group inside the Delivery Operations Hub, and is never presented as a separate surface.
No Workflow content is renderable on the Frontline Worker Application unless it belongs to a Workflow version that completed all three approval stages.
Every published version carries a mandatory republish description stored in the permanent version history.

No agent, capability, or composed behaviour authored or configured in the Studio goes live without passing its evaluation scenarios. The evaluation gate is hard, always, for every tenant, and binds every operator including the root account.
No user interface control anywhere in the Studio creates, edits, or deletes an atomic capability. Tenants never author atoms; adding a capability is an engineering change in the foundation.
Every Studio action that changes state writes its audit event in the same transaction, and fails if the audit write fails. An action that cannot be audited does not happen.

The Studio originates no command-channel command directly. The command channel carries exactly five classes: lot release, reassignment or substitution, qualification clearance, suspension, and version change.
No Studio view describes a published version as in force on a device; a published version is not in force until the version-change command reaches applied on that device.
A Run never starts against a partially built or unverified work package; a partial package could omit a severity mapping and thereby omit a hold.
Severity classification and Severity 1 hold placement occur on the device at the instant of capture, including fully offline, in every test configuration.
No artificial-intelligence component in or reachable from the Studio can classify a deviation or assign a severity. Detection is rule-based and runs on the worker's device.
Nothing is machine-translated at run time on any surface.
Severity must be set explicitly on every screen that can deviate; publication is blocked otherwise, naming each unmapped screen. The platform never assumes a value.
Mapping a band to Severity 1 presents the arming confirmation and records the author's explicit confirmation; if the confirmation cannot be recorded, the mapping is not saved.
Every Workflow carries exactly one Job Type; no platform behaviour is conditioned on the presence or value of a Service Type tag.
business_rules.enforcement_point: FUNC-STU-03-02-C-1, validated at save and again at publication

business_rules.statement: A Workflow carries exactly four settings and exactly two inheritable defaults; no third inheritable default exists. Deviation severity is never a workflow default.
The published sequence-detection reference is identical to the drawn screen order and branch targets, with no separate authoring path.
A soft proof gate never alters specification-gate behaviour in any test configuration. The specification gate is hard platform-wide and no author or tenant setting can configure it away.
One screen in the Builder corresponds to exactly one screen on the device and one unit of execution telemetry; no sub-screen construct exists.
A Shared Instruction Block is scoped to exactly one Workflow and appears nowhere in the Content Libraries; cross-Workflow reference is refused at the service layer.
Screens hold pointers to library items and never copies; an item cannot be archived while screens reference it, and the referencing screens are named.
Retrieval applies a metadata filter before semantic ranking in every configuration, so a torque clip cannot surface on a paint screen.
An escalation routing template names roles only, and no user interface or application programming interface path permits naming an individual. Only two channels exist: in-app and email.
No work package, in any configuration, contains a Training Library item. Viewing training content produces no run telemetry, no production record, and no qualification.
No practice-mode capability exists in any surface. Practice mode is cut from scope; if it resurfaces it is handled as a change request.
Required captures, gates, specification limits, and severity mappings are byte-identical across all three difficulty levels; the level changes the depth of explanation only.
A fully covered screen carries six reviewed renderings — three levels by two locales; the completeness check blocks publication otherwise.
The platform mints the part identifier; no author input influences it. The inline mini-form accepts a name and nothing else.
A part reference is attached only after the registry confirms creation; a reference to a part that does not exist would break genealogy.
No content reaches a published version without three recorded transitions by three distinct identities. The Reviewer cannot edit content. The Release Authority cannot be bypassed.
business_rules.enforcement_point: MOD-STU-11 chain, enforced at the service layer

business_rules.statement: A person holding multiple roles cannot occupy two stages on one submission; distinctness is evaluated by identity, not by role.
A mis-classified patch is returned by the Reviewer; a change to limits, gates, timing, severity mappings, sequence, or screen count cannot be published as a patch.
An in-flight Run's pinned package is never swapped by any publication; a run finishes on the workflow version it started on.
A version is never auto-archived; archival requires a deliberate action against a clear no-active-Jobs indicator.

The qualification gate is the only gate whose enforcement posture a tenant may change, and it can only be made stricter than the platform floor. Specification and evaluation gates are hard and non-configurable.
Qualification validation runs at assignment, at Run start, and at every override-carrying screen.
A certification-requirement change grandfathers active assignments with a flag, a supervisor confirmation, and a recorded reason; it applies to Runs scheduled after the carrying version is published.
No surface shows a clearance as effective before its command reaches applied on the device.
The server mirrors an on-device classification and never re-decides it. Server-side atoms are the mirror and confirmation path, never the trigger.
The Agent Builder composes reasoning agents only; no path composes an action agent. Action agents ship as platform-provided templates the tenant configures.
A composed agent reaches production only after the evaluation gate, the tenant approval chain, and platform review, in that order.
Lane A changes no configured value in any configuration, and every Lane-A refinement is logged and reversible.
No Lane-B proposal is ever auto-approved; the decision is human and made exactly once, in the Client Command Center.
There is no on/off switch for learning anywhere on the platform; the approval queue is the control and Lane A changes no configured value.
Nothing learned is shared across tenants or exported as external training data, at any privilege level.
An incomplete locale blocks publication in that locale, with each missing element named; where the completeness check cannot run, publication is blocked entirely.
No tenant configuration can widen the separation-of-duties floor: an author never approves their own work and the Release Authority is never bypassed.
Where the identity layer is unreachable, the Studio fails closed to published read at most.

decisions.question: The identity and naming of the five standard report data sets; §4.10.5 names set 4 differently from §6.12.1.
options: (a) adopt the §4.10.5 name, "Clearance (qualification-override) frequency by role"
(b) adopt the §6.12.1 name, "Override frequency by role"
(c) adopt "Clearance frequency by role" with the parenthetical dropped once tenants are familiar with the term
decisions.impact: Reporting terminology is evidence in a quality audit; the identity of all five sets remains open.

decisions.question: Whether a reconnecting device uploads captures before or after pulling commands.
options: commands first (safety)
captures first (data integrity)
decisions.adopted_working_position: reconnection runs in three phases — stop-class commands pulled and applied first, then every pending capture uploaded with nothing discarded, then enabling-class commands applied
decisions.status: adopted working position (2026-08-14), client ratification outstanding
decisions.impact: Determines reconnection ordering; payload detail deferred to the Frontline Functional Specification.

decisions.question: Surface name divergence between the Statement of Work and the blueprint commission (Delivery Operations Hub vs Digital Operations Hub).
options: Delivery Operations Hub
Digital Operations Hub
decisions.impact: Naming across all documentation and interfaces.

decisions.question: Whether the Site level is mandatory or an open drafting recommendation.
options: mandatory
open drafting recommendation
decisions.adopted_working_position: adopted 2026-08-14 as mandatory, with a default Site auto-created at tenant provisioning; both source readings preserved in the card
decisions.impact: Hierarchy depth floor; the Site level can never be configured away.

decisions.question: Whether a Job binds to one Area as a hard constraint or to one parent node at the configured depth.
options: one Area hard constraint
one parent node at the configured depth
decisions.adopted_working_position: adopted 2026-08-14 as one parent node per Job at the tenant's configured depth
decisions.impact: Job binding; field-level definition still gated on DEC-UNIT-001.

decisions.question: Whether soft suspension lifts on an operator signal or on a payment event the platform is elsewhere stated not to receive.
options: operator signal
payment event
decisions.adopted_working_position: adopted 2026-08-14 as the explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console, with no payment event observed and the integration path left open and unbuilt
decisions.impact: Suspension lift mechanism.

decisions.question: Whether the finish window's 24-hour floor and 7-day ceiling are settled or open drafting values.
options: settled
open drafting values
decisions.impact: Record-finish window bounds in the settings register.

decisions.question: Three-stage approval versus Lane B auto-publication: does an approved Lane-B patch still require Reviewer and Release Authority?
options: (a) the chain is absolute and a Lane-B patch must still pass Reviewer and Release Authority
(b) the Lane-B decision by a Quality Manager in the Client Command Center is the human sign-off and substitutes for the chain
decisions.status: open — recommendation is reading (b) restricted to values that cannot alter a specification limit, a severity mapping, or a gate rule
decisions.impact: Whether a specification-adjacent value reaches the floor with one approver.

decisions.question: The meaning of the Supervisor+ and QM+ forms across five additive, non-hierarchical roles.
options: additive union of the named roles
ranked hierarchy
decisions.adopted_working_position: This blueprint reads the shorthand as an additive union of the named roles rather than a ranked hierarchy
decisions.impact: Authority matrix interpretation across the blueprint.

decisions.question: Plant Manager and Quality Director as personas or roles; §5.18's fixed-role table includes Plant Manager while §3.5 fixes five roles.
options: §3.5's five fixed roles
§5.18's inclusion of Plant Manager as a row in a fixed-role table
decisions.adopted_working_position: This blueprint treats Plant Manager as a persona whose Studio access is delivered by a Supervisor role without the authoring grant
decisions.impact: Role model and Studio permission matrix.

decisions.question: Confirmation of the nobody-on-shift escalation default.
options: tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery
decisions.adopted_working_position: recommended as the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery
decisions.impact: An authored template whose roles are all off-shift at 03:00 delivers nothing unless settled.

decisions.question: Confirmation of 24-month anonymisation under the no-purge model.
decisions.impact: Retention and anonymisation lifecycle.

decisions.question: Archived-data retrieval expectation.
decisions.impact: Archived data access.

decisions.question: Which compliance standards mandate deletion.
decisions.impact: Deletion obligations.

decisions.question: The canonical names and codes of the eight starter Job Types and eight starter Service Type tags, which are not stated anywhere in the Statement of Work.
options: (a) the client supplies the sixteen names and codes before build
(b) the platform ships a provisional set marked provisional and the client replaces it during onboarding
(c) the platform ships with an empty seeded set and every tenant creates its own
decisions.adopted_working_position: the platform-seeded catalogue ships empty at version 1, tenants create their own Job Types and Service Type tags immediately at every tier with no platform approval step, and the sixteen entries are loaded into the seeded catalogue when the client supplies them, inherited read-only and overwriting no tenant-created entry
decisions.impact: Delivery Operations Hub filters Workflow selection by Job Type; wrong or missing list makes selection unusable at go-live.

decisions.question: The owed unit-model engineering paper, which gates the data-model appendix.
decisions.impact: Gates the data-model appendix and DEC-AREA-001's field-level definition.

decisions.question: The Standards and Operations Studio module count; the Statement of Work provides no canonical module count.
options: eighteen modules, one per numbered section of Part V
a six-module functional grouping (rejected)
a nine-module grouping mirroring the nine screen configuration sections (rejected)
a twenty-two-module grouping (rejected)
decisions.adopted_working_position: One module per numbered section of Part V, in section order, with the section's own heading as the module name — exactly eighteen modules, MOD-STU-01 through MOD-STU-18
decisions.status: Client Decision Required — derived, not sourced
decisions.impact: Changes labels and navigation grouping, not any rule about who may author, review, release, or publish.

decisions.question: The Read-only Auditor's Studio access; the §5.18 table omits ROLE-TEN-AUD entirely.
options: (a) no Studio access, working entirely from the Delivery Operations Hub audit log and PDF exports
(b) read-only Studio access limited to published versions, version history, approval logs, and diffs, with no access to drafts or in-review versions
(c) read-only Studio access to everything including drafts
decisions.status: open — newly identified; every Read-only Auditor cell in the chapter reads Client Decision Required rather than being guessed
decisions.impact: Auditor evidence access to approval log, screen-level diff and version history.

decisions.question: Whether Coaching Corpus content crosses the platform boundary to be embedded, under what data-processing terms, in which region, and how model deprecation is handled.
options: (a) embed in-region under a data-processing agreement with no retention by the model provider
(b) embed only non-identifiable asset types and exclude video containing identifiable workers from semantic indexing
(c) run an in-boundary embedding model, accepting a quality difference
decisions.impact: Sending video of identifiable workers to an external model is a data-processing and compliance question.

decisions.question: Recovery Time Objective and Recovery Point Objective values, not specified in the Statement of Work for any surface.
options: a stringent pair (RTO one hour, RPO five minutes)
a moderate pair (four hours, one hour)
a relaxed pair (next business day, twenty-four hours)
decisions.impact: Recommendation: moderate pair for the Studio, stringent pair for the Delivery Operations Hub.

decisions.question: Whether the recommended Studio monitoring metrics are exposed to tenants in the Studio or held platform-side only.
options: exposed to tenants in the Studio
held platform-side only
decisions.impact: Monitoring visibility.

decisions.question: Who may enable a capability in the Atomic Capability area; §5.15.2 says 'an authorised user' without naming the role.
options: (a) the Quality Manager only
(b) the Tenant Admin only
(c) the Agent Author capability holder
decisions.status: open — newly proposed; recommendation is option (b) with mandatory Quality Manager consultation recorded
decisions.impact: Enabling/disabling a capability changes configuration surfaces across every Workflow and can block publication.

decisions.question: Whether the Prevention Agent and Deviation and Containment Agent are governed by pre-authorised Studio-authored policy or by a runtime human gate.
options: §5.2/§3.7: pre-authorised, Studio-authored policy
§8.3.2/§8.3.3: every action agent routes through a human gate before any effect; Prevention Agent labelled 'action, gated'
decisions.adopted_working_position: gating per agent in the agent record's governance-binding field: the Prevention Agent carries `authoring-time policy`, the Deviation and Containment Agent carries `runtime human gate` for proposals beyond pre-authorised containment
decisions.impact: The Studio must author the pre-authorised policy completely and never present it as a runtime human gate.

decisions.question: Whether the containment checklist is launched by the device locally or by the Deviation and Containment Agent server-side.
options: §3.4/§7.9.1 layer b: on the device, locally and offline-capable
§5.2.2/§5.7.1: attributed to the agent, which §7.9.1 layer c places server-side and online-only
decisions.adopted_working_position: Option A: the device launches the pre-authorised containment checklist locally, from the version-pinned work package, at the instant of classification, with no network required, and the Deviation and Containment Agent enriches the deviation brief afterwards and never triggers the checklist
decisions.status: adopted working position (2026-08-14), safer reading; source disagreement recorded at section 51.11A
decisions.impact: A checklist step requiring a server lookup cannot be a launch-time step.

decisions.question: Cross-reference defect: §5.2.2 cites '(5.5.9)' for the Severity 1 arming disclosure but the correct section is §5.5.8.
options: correct the cross-reference to §5.5.8
decisions.impact: Downstream requirement traceability keyed on the cited section number would point at the wrong configuration section.

decisions.question: Which tenant role may create, edit, deprecate, and archive a custom Job Type or Service Type tag.
options: Quality Manager only
Tenant Admin only in the tenant administration area
either
decisions.status: open — newly proposed; recommendation is Tenant Admin in the tenant administration area with the Quality Manager consulted
decisions.impact: An uncontrolled custom Job Type list degrades Workflow selection on the floor.

decisions.question: The fate of an archived version: can it be un-archived, linked to a new Job, or is archival reversible at all?
options: (a) archival is reversible by the Quality Manager with an audited reason
(b) archival is irreversible and a new version must be created from the archived content
(c) archival is reversible only within a stated window
decisions.impact: A tenant that archives the wrong version has no stated remedy.

decisions.question: Which seven capture types exist at launch; §1.7/§7.8.3 and §5.5.3 list different sets.
options: §1.7/§7.8.3: measurement, scan, photo, checklist, boolean, electronic signature, free text
§5.5.3: measurement entry, photo capture, barcode or QR scan, checkbox confirmation, digital signature, free text, dropdown selection
decisions.adopted_working_position: The adopted working position is the §5.5.3 set: measurement entry, photo capture, barcode or Quick Response code scan, checkbox confirmation, digital signature, free text, and dropdown selection, plus none for instruction-only screens
decisions.status: adopted working position — Derived Clarification, never SoW Fact; ratification owner is the client's product owner with the platform architect
decisions.impact: A Frontline player cannot render a type the contract does not name; an author could publish a screen the device cannot render.

decisions.question: The deployed scanner hardware list that a tool barcode scan depends on, owed by the client.
decisions.impact: An authored tool-barcode requirement that no deployed scanner can read would block a screen on the floor.

decisions.question: Whether a Content Library edit reaches an in-flight Run (pointer semantics) or waits for the next package build (pinning semantics).
options: (a) pointer semantics — resolution at the moment the checklist launches, so an in-flight Run gets the new version
(b) pinning semantics — the package carries the checklist as resolved at build time, so an in-flight Run keeps the old version until its next package
decisions.status: open — recommendation is pinning semantics for anything that ships in the package
decisions.impact: Two behaviours with different audit consequences for which policy was in force during a run.

decisions.question: What the 'lightweight review' of §5.7.4 for edits to published Content Library items removes relative to the three-stage chain.
options: (a) the full three-stage chain with a scoped preview limited to the changed item
(b) Author plus a single Reviewer with release authority folded into the review
(c) library content governed by its own two-stage chain defined separately
decisions.adopted_working_position: Until it is decided, this blueprint treats library edits as passing the full chain and records the divergence
decisions.impact: Whether the separation-of-duties floor differs between two kinds of content that both reach the floor.

decisions.question: Whether the offline package carries all three difficulty levels or only the assigned worker's selected level.
options: (a) carry all three levels, the current package definition
(b) carry only the assigned worker's level and require a re-pull on substitution, which fails offline
(c) carry the assigned worker's level plus the standard level as a substitution fallback
decisions.adopted_working_position: Until it resolves, the package definition carries instruction content at all levels (the source's stated interim rule)
decisions.impact: Package payload size versus offline mid-Run worker substitution rendering.

decisions.question: The review interval for an incomplete skeletal part record.
options: no reminder
a fixed platform interval
a tenant-configurable interval
decisions.status: open — newly proposed; recommendation a tenant-configurable interval defaulting to seven days
decisions.impact: An accumulation of name-only stubs degrades the registry's usefulness for genealogy and reporting.

decisions.question: Minimum staffing for a complete approval chain and who is eligible for a per-workflow Release Authority override.
options: (a) require at least two holders of a Release-Authority-capable role at tenant scope, enforced at Workflow submission
(b) permit the per-workflow override to name any authoring-grant holder who is not the Author or the Reviewer
(c) permit the Reviewer stage to be performed by a second Quality Manager only
decisions.status: open — newly proposed; recommendation option (a) with a pre-submission staffing check
decisions.impact: A tenant with one Quality Manager and one authoring-grant holder can author and review but cannot release — a silent operational deadlock.

decisions.question: The authoritative field-by-field assignment of which values are package-borne versus server-only, which Part VII does not enumerate.
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required; decision owner the platform architect
decisions.impact: Without it an approved Lane-B value cannot be routed deterministically to the patch-publication path or the immediate-application path.

decisions.question: Device storage-full behaviour, explicitly deferred to the Frontline functional specification.
decisions.status: open — explicitly deferred; no behaviour invented
decisions.impact: Package coaching-asset omission behaviour under storage pressure.

decisions.question: Deprecation, disablement, rollback of a deployed composed agent, and the fate of its in-flight runs.
options: (a) a tenant-side disable control on the composed agent with immediate effect and an audited reason
(b) disablement only through the platform console
(c) a versioned composed-agent lifecycle mirroring Workflow versioning with rollback to a prior composition
decisions.status: open — recommendation option (a) for disablement plus option (c) for versioning
decisions.impact: A misbehaving composed reasoning agent has no stated off switch short of the platform-wide emergency pause.

decisions.question: Who decides a Lane-B proposal: §5.16.3 says Quality Engineer or Quality Manager; §3.8 and the closed action set say Quality Manager and above.
options: (a) Quality Manager and above only
(b) the authoring grant confers Lane-B decision authority
(c) Quality Manager only for package-borne values and authoring-grant holders for server-only values
decisions.impact: Widening Lane-B authority to the Supervisor role changes who can alter operating values on the floor.

decisions.question: The taxonomy versioning approach, confirmed by the platform team alongside DEC-TAX-002.
decisions.impact: How replacement of provisional taxonomy names is versioned.

decisions.question: Referenced alongside DEC-EMBED-001 as a decision owned by the client's platform team with legal counsel.
decisions.impact: Compliance certification posture.

contradictions.description: §4.10.5 names report set 4 'Clearance (qualification-override) frequency by role'; §6.12.1 names the same set 'Override frequency by role'. §4.10.5 also marks all five identities open while stating count and ownership as fixed.
conflicting_values: count and ownership fixed vs identity open

contradictions.description: The Statement of Work's Studio permission table (§5.18) is headed 'Fixed role' and includes Plant Manager, which §3.5 states is not a role and fixes exactly five roles.
conflicting_values: §5.18's Plant Manager row in a fixed-role table

contradictions.description: The §5.18 Studio permission table omits the Read-only Auditor (ROLE-TEN-AUD) entirely, so the source states nothing about that role's Studio access.
conflicting_values: read-only access to published versions/history/approval logs/diffs
read-only access to everything including drafts

contradictions.description: The Statement of Work uses Supervisor+ and Quality Manager+ without defining an ordering across five additive, non-hierarchical roles.
conflicting_values: additive union of the named roles

contradictions.description: §5.2/§3.7 govern the Prevention and Deviation Agents by pre-authorised Studio-authored policy; §8.3.2 states every action agent routes through a human gate and §8.3.3 labels the Prevention Agent 'action, gated'.
conflicting_values: runtime human gate before any effect

contradictions.description: §3.4 and §7.9.1 layer b place the containment checklist launch on the device, locally and offline-capable; §5.2.2 and §5.7.1 attribute the launch to the agent, which §7.9.1 layer c places server-side and online-only.
conflicting_values: device launches locally from the pinned package
the Deviation and Containment Agent launches server-side

contradictions.description: Source cross-reference defect: §5.2.2 cites '(5.5.9)' for the Severity 1 arming disclosure, but §5.5.1's table and §5.11's numbering place Deviation Rules and Severity Mapping at §5.5.8, with §5.5.9 being Tool and Equipment.
DEC-TAX-002 option (c), an empty seeded set with every tenant creating its own, contradicts §5.3.2's statement that the platform seeds eight Job Types and eight Service Type tags.
conflicting_values: seeded catalogue ships empty at version 1

contradictions.description: Both the platform canon and the Studio state seven capture types at launch, but the two sets differ: §1.7/§7.8.3 list checklist and boolean; §5.5.3 lists checkbox confirmation and dropdown selection.
conflicting_values: measurement, scan, photo, checklist, boolean, electronic signature, free text
measurement entry, photo capture, barcode or QR scan, checkbox confirmation, digital signature, free text, dropdown selection

contradictions.description: §5.7 states a library edit propagates immediately to every referencing screen; §5.14 and Part II state a Run's work package is pinned at assignment and never re-based. The in-flight interaction is not stated.
conflicting_values: pointer semantics — resolution at launch time
pinning semantics — package carries the checklist as resolved at build time

contradictions.description: §5.7.4 introduces a 'lightweight review' for edits to published Content Library items; §5.11.1 states no Workflow content reaches the frontline without explicit human sign-off at each of the three stages and §5.8 requires 'the same approval chain'.
conflicting_values: full three-stage chain at each stage

contradictions.description: §5.11.1 requires human sign-off at each of three stages; §5.16.3 and §6.7.4 have an approved Lane-B proposal auto-publish a patch version with 'no second approval, no ceremony', and §5.12.1 lists a Lane-B-approved value as a PATCH class change.
conflicting_values: single Lane-B human decision substitutes for the chain

contradictions.description: §5.16.3 states a Quality Engineer or Quality Manager decides a Lane-B proposal; §3.8 and the Client Command Center closed action set state the learned-change decision is Quality Manager and above.

The discovery-stage description of offline deviations being 'processed at sync, with severity-band evaluation running on the captured value at that point' is explicitly superseded by Part V: evaluation happens at capture; only escalation delivery happens at sync.
conflicting_values: evaluation at capture, delivery at sync (superseding)

contradictions.description: §5.15.2 says 'an authorised user' enables capabilities without naming a role, while §5.15.4 names the Agent Author capability specifically for compose authority.
The submission, review and approval path for a composed agent is stated, but deprecation, disablement, rollback of a deployed composed agent and the fate of its in-flight runs are not.
conflicting_values: disablement only through the platform console

contradictions.description: §5.3.2 grants custom Job Type and Service Type creation to 'tenants' without naming a role, leaving the authorship of a taxonomy that shapes Delivery Operations Hub Workflow-selection filtering unassigned.
§6.7.4 states the authoritative package-borne versus server-only field assignment is carried in the Part VII package contract; Part VII does not enumerate it.
conflicting_values: Part VII does not enumerate it

contradictions.description: §5.9 leaves open whether the offline package carries all three difficulty levels or only the assigned worker's selected level; the interim rule carries all levels.
conflicting_values: assigned level plus standard as a substitution fallback

contradictions.description: The Statement of Work states prior versions are permanently readable and archival is deliberate and manual, but does not state whether an archived version can be un-archived or linked to a new Job.
conflicting_values: reversible by the Quality Manager with an audited reason
reversible only within a stated window

contradictions.description: The chapter names the operational system of record the Delivery Operations Hub (SoW §1.2, Part IV heading); the blueprint commission refers to it as the 'Digital Operations Hub'.

The three-stage chain requires three distinct people, and Release Authority defaults to the Quality Manager, but no minimum staffing is stated, producing a silent operational deadlock for a tenant with one Quality Manager and one authoring-grant holder.
conflicting_values: separation of duties satisfied by any second holder of the approving role (§3.5)

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Regulated-Industry mode flag cannot be read
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The last known value with its age
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Stricter interpretation: treat the tenant as being in Regulated-Industry mode
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The mode applied as on, with the mode-status panel stating the posture is precautionary pending confirmation
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A fresh state read; reconciliation replays tenant_state_history and asserts the applied posture matched the true posture for every minute of the outage

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A standard report data set cannot compute
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Presenting the last successfully computed result with its data-as-of timestamp and an explicit pending state, never as current; then presenting the underlying records
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The report is unavailable and says so; no operational behaviour depends on a report
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Recomputation; reconciliation compares against last delivered figures and flags material differences as corrections

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A bulk parts upload fails validation
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Rejection of the whole file with a downloadable per-row, per-column error report and no partial import
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Manual single-record entry through the registry screen; then the Studio inline-add seam
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No records are created and the tenant's existing registry is untouched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A corrected re-upload; reconciliation asserts the part-count delta equals the accepted row count exactly

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The conflict-resolution path fails: conflicts arrive but cannot be resolved or routed
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Hold every affected write in a quarantine state rather than applying either version
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Human escalation to the Quality Manager, who holds the resolve authority; then the run's Summary is marked uncomputed under FB-DOH-COMPUTE-006
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Quarantined data, an uncomputed Summary and a run held visibly in the review queue — nothing lost, nothing guessed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Human resolution; reconciliation asserts every conflict event has either an automatic or a human resolution record

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Super Admin tenant-configuration registry is unreachable so a value's floor cannot be validated
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Refuse the write; then the tenant administration area enters read-only with an explanatory banner
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Every setting keeps its last validated value, which is by definition at or stricter than the floor
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Registry restoration; reconciliation re-validates every current tenant setting and reports any value looser than its floor

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Studio session connectivity loss or save failure
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Explicit disconnected state, local draft buffer, submit disabled, no save claimed
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The browser session ends or the local draft buffer is lost
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Last durably persisted draft revision; published versions untouched; no partial draft enters the approval chain
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Field-level accept-or-discard reconciliation with no silent merge, written to the tenant audit log in the same transaction

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Bounded idempotent retry re-using the submission identifier
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No version number minted; prior published version remains in force
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconcile minted version numbers against audit entries; a version number is never re-used

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Submission waits in the Approval Queue with an ageing indicator
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Content stays unpublished; the floor continues on the prior version

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Content Library or semantic index unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Existing pointers retained, section read-only, library named
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No pointer cleared; submission blocked for affected screens
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Pointer re-validation before submission is re-enabled; archived-item pointers named for replacement

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Manual authoring path fully open; specific assistance named as unavailable; no silent retry
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The assistance remains unavailable for the session
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Content authored manually; curated coaching defaults carry coaching
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Index rebuilt by backfill for assets approved during the outage; the learning view reports the backlog explicitly

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Bounded idempotent rebuild, then supervisor on-demand re-pull
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Run cannot start on that device; the device says so plainly; a Run never starts against a partial package
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Successful re-pull; reconciliation confirms the package hash matches the definition, any mismatch quarantines rather than executes

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Upstream dependency unavailable: registry, entitlements, severity catalog, parts, workers
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Last-retrieved state shown with its retrieval timestamp, labelled last retrieved
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No prior state available for this session
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Dependent configuration surfaces frozen read-only; publication blocked
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-read registry and entitlement set; re-evaluate every open draft's capability dependencies before permitting submission

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Evaluation harness or platform review unavailable for a composed agent
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Composed agent held at its current governance stage with the stage named
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Agent not deployed; the evaluation gate is never bypassed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-submission produces a recorded outcome; no state was inferred during the outage

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Validation service unavailable: locale completeness, qualification cross-check, capability dependency
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Publication blocked, failing closed, with the specific check named
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Nothing published; prior version remains in force
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Coverage grid recomputed; every changed element listed by element and locale

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Bounded idempotent retry of the whole transaction
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Surface the failure with the action explicitly marked as not performed
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Action does not happen; state unchanged; user told the action was not performed; no version number minted
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-attempt on user command only; reconciliation compares minted version numbers against audit entries

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Studio surface is unreachable or its persistence layer rejects writes
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Authors held in a read-only degraded view of already-published content; drafts protected by the FB-STU-01 local draft buffer
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The read-only view cannot render because the content service itself is down
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Authoring is suspended. Every already-published Workflow version remains in force. Every already-built work package remains pinned. Runs continue.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Authors resume from the last durably saved draft revision; the platform reports the exact draft revision restored and the exact edits not recovered

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A built work package fails integrity verification
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Quarantine — the suspect item is set aside where it cannot be used but is not destroyed
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The package is Quarantined and never Delivered; the Run cannot start on that device with the failing element named
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Rebuild and hash reconciliation against the package definition for the pinned version
